Prometheus labs has access to superscience, so maybe they could build a robot body that would be compatible with a biological human brain, but it would probably be cheaper and easier to grow clones and prevent their brains from developing (and even cheaper and easier to just grow regular clones and chop their brains out).

Think about how much harder it is to make an egg or an apple artificially than it is to just grow them, then scale that up to a whole human body. I'm not saying these fictional superscientists couldn't do it, just that it would be a pretty differnt thing at that point.

item.content:encoded:
For some behind the scenes action with the Omega-K Family:

Before the brain transplants there was the talk about brains. What to do with em? Eventually, it came down to two options. Brain swapping through wave transfer, or through surgery. After team-member Galaxy-Class mysteriously vanished, I took on the role of figuring out what to do with de brainz. Time passes and here we are.

Narratively, this is done for emotional impact as well as imagery. There's more to play with and a lot more to tie in with some of the themes of this team.

In-Universe, the reason is $. Repairing the same body as it ages through point DNA modifications and so on is more expensive than what is essentially a hackjob+lego. Furthermore, repairing a body gives you youth back, but also YOUR youth back. Wouldn't you rather want something different? And if you have the money why wait? You can easily just change into something more…experimental.

In any case, I hope you enjoyed the piece!
